title: Stop, stabilize, signal

action.text: Pause on stable ground and check the scene before approaching an injured person. Check responsiveness, breathing and obvious life-threatening injury.
If someone is unresponsive, breathing abnormally or bleeding severely, call 911 and follow the dispatcher. Give your location and the immediate hazard.
If travel has stopped, use available shelter and insulation. Tell everyone where to wait and who is trying to make contact.

verify.text: Each person can name the immediate hazard, the group's location or last known point, and who is attempting contact.

stop.text: Leave immediate danger by a clearly safer path. If location and safe travel are uncertain, stay findable and seek help.

title: Assess before you move

action.text: Inventory the group, the weather, the remaining daylight and the last place you can identify confidently.
Compare what you see with a mapped trail, junction or other reliable feature. Record the last verified place if your current location is uncertain.
Move only when the group can name a safe next checkpoint and is able to reach it. Keep current conditions and the slowest member in the decision.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Use location, daylight and group condition to decide whether travel makes sense.
applies: A stopped group with a potentially safe route and enough time to assess.
equipment: Offline map or paper map, watch, light and weather information if available.

verify.text: Before stepping off, someone can point to the next checkpoint and explain how the party will know it has reached it.

stop.text: Weather, terrain or group condition can invalidate a previously reasonable route. Halt if the next checkpoint becomes uncertain.

diagram: Last verified place | Check group and conditions | Name a safe next point
visual: Route-confidence decision schematic with three checkpoints.

title: Stay, signal or move

action.text: Stop. If an immediate hazard threatens the spot, reach safer ground nearby only when you can identify a safe way there.
Contact 911 when help is needed and service is available. Report last known position, landmarks, number of people, injuries and any planned movement.
If you cannot determine a safe route, stay together in a findable location, shelter from weather and prepare to signal when responders are nearby.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Make an explicit choice between staying findable and moving to a known safe position.
applies: Lost or overdue outdoor party. Immediate danger and known route are separate questions.
equipment: Phone or emergency communicator, whistle, light, bright material and weather protection if available.

verify.text: Your location description gives responders a usable starting point. Mark a plan change in your message if you must move.

stop.text: Never attempt an uncertain shortcut over water or ice to reach a signal or a road.

diagram: Immediate danger? | Safe route known? | If uncertain, stay findable
visual: Two-question decision sequence with a stay-put outcome.

title: Leave a usable trip plan
origin: B014 reconstruction R01 and B012 P02

action.text: Record the starting point, planned route and return time. Include names or party size and expected vehicle location if relevant.
Give the plan to a trusted contact and agree on the overdue reporting point and what information to pass to responders.
Carry a copy and notify the contact of significant changes when you can. Check back in at return.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending

applies: A trip outside dependable cell service, especially an unfamiliar trail.
equipment: Paper plan or saved message, mapped route, and contact information.

verify.text: Your contact can identify the trailhead and say when they should act.

stop.text: If nobody can act on an overdue report, reconsider the route and exposure before departing.

title: Pack by failure mode
origin: NPS Ten Essentials; new manuscript

action.text: Map darkness, navigation loss, exposure and delayed return to independent kit functions. Consider Sun protection and repair supplies as conditions warrant.
Check each function at home: a light turns on, the map works offline, the shelter can be set up, and spare insulation is dry.
Give shared gear an owner. Ensure the group can reach critical pieces without emptying all the packs.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Match kit functions to foreseeable failures and practice using them.
applies: Day and overnight travel. Terrain, temperature and time without help shape the kit.
equipment: Map, light, insulation, shelter, water, food, first aid and other route-appropriate essentials.

verify.text: Simulate one failure and retrieve the correct item without a signal or a search through loose gear.

stop.text: Narrow or postpone the trip if critical protection or navigation is absent.

title: Set a turnaround before departure
origin: B014 P18 and B012 P02

action.text: Identify a decision point and latest turnaround time. Build in daylight and delay margin for the slowest group member.
At each reliable checkpoint compare actual progress and conditions with the plan. Recalculate when the return route or pace changes.
Turn back early if visibility, access, group condition or the return margin deteriorates and the return route is known safe.

objective: Preserve the time and energy needed to return.
applies: An out-and-back trip where conditions, group speed or daylight can change.
equipment: Watch, map and reliable forecast or local advisory.

verify.text: The group can name the trigger and the place where it will reassess.

stop.text: If the return route is no longer safe or known, use the stay/signal decision rather than a guessed shortcut.

diagram: Set return margin | Compare at checkpoints | Turn back while able
visual: A decision occurs before the intended destination when the return margin is lost.

title: Give rescuers a usable location
origin: B013 P13 and B014 P16

action.text: Give the site or park name plus trailhead, road, junction or other verified landmark. If sending coordinates, read the format shown by the device.
State how many people are involved, whether anyone is injured and what nearby hazards affect access.
Specify whether you will wait or must move. Follow dispatcher directions and communicate changes if you can.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Report what you know and identify uncertainty explicitly.
applies: Calling for rescue at an outdoor emergency in the United States.
equipment: Phone or suitable communicator, offline map and light if available.

verify.text: Ask whether your location was received and which approach the responder wants you to use, if any.

stop.text: Avoid moving solely to improve service if the route is uncertain or hazardous.

diagram: Give verified location | Describe people and hazards | Confirm follow-up
visual: Dispatch handoff sequence with known location separated from uncertain information.

title: Keep track of everyone
origin: NPS Hike Smart and B014 P17

action.text: Choose a route and pace that the whole group can manage. Agree that nobody leaves a junction before the group is accounted for.
Check attendance at the start, at junctions and before leaving a long stop. Give the back of the group a way to signal the front.
If someone is missing, keep the remaining group together. Record the last place and time where the person was seen and contact responders when needed.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Prevent unplanned separation before it becomes a search.
applies: Group travel on land in uneven terrain, variable visibility or busy trail networks.
equipment: Group roster or head count, paper or offline map and an agreed signal.

verify.text: Everyone knows the next checkpoint and the count agrees at every major stop.

stop.text: Avoid splitting into an uncoordinated search. Follow directions from responders.

diagram: Count at departure | Recount at junctions | Record last known point
visual: The count belongs at points where separation is likely.

title: Prepare a communication backup
origin: NPS Ten Essentials and B014 P15/P16

action.text: Save the route, emergency numbers and trip information before leaving coverage. Carry a paper copy independent of the phone battery.
Check how your equipment works before the trip and agree on an overdue trigger with a contact. A signal device helps nearby responders but cannot promise that someone knows your location.
If no message can get through, avoid uncertain travel just to find signal. Prepare to be located using known landmarks, shelter and available signals.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Keep a way to share essential information if a primary device fails.
applies: Trips without dependable voice or data service.
equipment: Phone, paper map and trip plan, whistle and light. Add a suitable emergency communicator if available.

verify.text: Demonstrate one location report and one backup signal while the phone is disconnected.

stop.text: Do not assume help has been dispatched if you cannot confirm that a message was received.

visual: The location record, overdue contact and signal serve different purposes.
reviewer: Search and rescue and communication equipment

title: Recognize the moment to call for help
origin: American Red Cross first aid; new manuscript

action.text: Look for ongoing danger before approaching. Observe responsiveness, breathing and life-threatening bleeding.
Call 911 for unresponsiveness, abnormal breathing or life-threatening bleeding. Give the exact location and describe what you see in plain language.
Follow the dispatcher and work within your training. If someone else is available, assign them to communicate and guide responders.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Recognize emergency signs and transfer clear information to EMS.
applies: Lay responder at a sudden injury or illness in the United States.
equipment: Phone or emergency communicator and first-aid equipment as available.

verify.text: State the emergency, location and access route. Confirm which person is calling.

stop.text: If the scene is unsafe, keep clear and give responders the hazard details.

diagram: Scene safety | Recognize emergency signs | Call and follow dispatcher
visual: A lay escalation pathway. Detailed first-aid procedures belong in Z10.

title: Stop at uncertain ice

action.text: Stop on stable land. Ice varies across one body of water; appearance, footsteps or a nearby measurement cannot establish your crossing.
Use a verified land route if conditions and group ability allow. If you cannot identify one, reassess time, exposure and communication from stable ground.
Share your location and the changed route or hold decision. Keep the group off the uncertain surface.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Preserve a safe land route when a winter shortcut is unverified.
applies: A walking party approaching a frozen lake, stream, flooded path or marsh.
equipment: Map and sufficient insulation and time for a safe alternative.

verify.text: The next segment stays on known ground and the group can describe its return option.

stop.text: An unverified shortcut, bridge approach or ice edge remains a stop point.

diagram: Stop on land | Identify a verified land option | Hold and seek help if uncertain
visual: Route decision for walking parties. Ice travel and rescue belong in the separate B013 chapters.
reviewer: Ice safety and search and rescue

title: Turn back at a flooded route
origin: FEMA flood guidance; new manuscript

action.text: Turn around before entering floodwater. Its depth and force may be difficult to judge and the road surface can be damaged.
Check local evacuation instructions and choose an official, open alternate route or safe higher location. Avoid relying on a previous crossing or another vehicle's tracks.
Report your updated position and route to the appropriate contact when you can. Call for emergency help if trapped.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Preserve an evacuation option when a familiar road or foot route floods.
applies: Rising or standing floodwater blocking a road, path or crossing.
equipment: Current emergency directions and a map for alternatives if available.

verify.text: A safe route is confirmed from reliable local information, or the group is waiting at a safer location.

stop.text: Do not drive or walk around a closure into floodwater.

diagram: Flooded road ahead | Turn around early | Use official route or higher ground
visual: Road closure is a stop condition, independent of the apparent depth.

title: Assess route, weather and group risk before departure
origin: MN DNR, NPS Hike Smart and NWS alerts; new manuscript

action.text: Review forecast temperatures, wind, precipitation, fire restrictions and any active Watches or Warnings for the exact route and elevation.
Match distance, elevation gain, terrain hazards and available daylight to the least experienced or slowest person in the group.
Identify bailout exits, water access and shelter points along the route, and define conditions that cancel or shorten the trip before departing.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Screen weather, terrain, daylight and group capability before committing to a route.
applies: Pre-departure planning for day or overnight outdoor travel across seasons. Conditions change rapidly and require re-checking at the trailhead.
equipment: Current forecast and alerts, topographic or trail map, daylight table and group health summary.

failure.text: Proceeding with an outdated forecast, overestimating daylight or assuming the group will speed up on unfamiliar terrain.

verify.text: Every participant can state the route length, expected return time, top weather hazard and pre-agreed cancellation trigger.

stop.text: Active Severe Weather Warnings, unresolved hazard closures or missing essential protection require postponing or changing the route.

title: Inspect critical gear before failure occurs
origin: NPS Ten Essentials and Ready.gov kit maintenance; new manuscript

action.text: Test lighting, communication devices and weather radio under battery power alone, and confirm offline maps open with airplane mode enabled.
Inspect shelter seams, poles, zippers, water containers, filter seals and first-aid expiration dates for wear, brittleness or missing parts.
Confirm cold-sensitive items such as batteries, fuel canisters and wet filters have thermal protection suited to forecast lows.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Detect degraded batteries, leaks, tears and expired supplies before entering the field.
applies: Routine pre-trip readiness check for backcountry packs and household emergency go-bags. Does not replace manufacturer servicing.
equipment: Packed kit, spare batteries, water containers, light, shelter, navigation tools and maintenance checklist.

failure.text: Discovering dead batteries, cracked water lids, missing tent poles or dried-out bandages only after stopping in poor weather.

verify.text: Every life-safety subsystem passes a live hands-on function test at home and is repacked in an accessible order.

stop.text: Replace or repair damaged shelter, navigation, light or water gear before departure, or cancel the outing until functional gear is ready.

title: Assign group roles and pacing boundaries
origin: NPS Hike Smart and Ready.gov planning; new manuscript

action.text: Designate a lead who sets a sustainable pace, a sweep who stays behind the last person, and a backup navigator carrying an independent map.
Establish mandatory regroup points at every trail junction, water crossing, steep climb and visibility drop before stepping off.
Rotate check-ins for hydration, warmth, foot comfort and morale so quieter or fatigued members can call a halt without social pressure.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Maintain clear leadership, head counts and mutual accountability during group travel or emergencies.
applies: Groups of two or more hikers, families or mixed-ability parties on land. Solo travelers use external check-in contacts instead.
equipment: Written group roster, agreed whistle signals, map copy for more than one person and shared emergency contact sheet.

failure.text: Unassigned leadership, fast walkers outpacing slower members past forks, or hidden fatigue going unreported until collapse.

verify.text: Every member knows who is lead, who is sweep, what whistle signal means stop and where the next regroup point lies.

stop.text: If the group loses visual or voice accountability or someone cannot sustain the pace safely, halt immediately, regroup and revise the objective.

title: Layer alert receivers and emergency messages
origin: Ready.gov alerts, plan and NOAA Weather Radio; new manuscript

action.text: Enable Wireless Emergency Alerts and local agency notifications, and carry a battery or hand-crank NOAA Weather Radio tested for local VHF reception.
Record an out-of-area contact, local meeting points and critical medical notes on waterproof paper so communication survives a dead phone.
Prefer short text messages over voice calls during network congestion, and conserve device battery by using low-power or airplane mode between checks.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Keep emergency warnings and outbound family coordination working when one communication network fails.
applies: Home preparedness and outdoor travel across areas with patchy cellular service or power outages.
equipment: Mobile phone with alerts enabled, battery or hand-crank NOAA Weather Radio, paper contact card and optional satellite communicator.

failure.text: Relying solely on a single smartphone battery or live data connection in a valley, storm or regional tower outage.

verify.text: Confirm NOAA Weather Radio receives the local broadcast and that every group member carries the written contact and meeting-point card.

stop.text: Never assume an unsent or unacknowledged message has triggered rescue; shift to stay-put visibility and physical signaling if contact fails.

title: Act on weather watches, warnings and abort triggers
origin: NWS flood, thunderstorm and Ready.gov evacuation guidance; new manuscript

action.text: Treat a Weather Watch as a trigger to review exits, shorten exposed routes and verify shelter options while conditions are still favorable.
Treat a Weather Warning, approaching thunder, rising runoff or rapid visibility loss as an immediate action threshold to seek proper shelter or evacuate.
Combine official alerts with on-site red flags—sudden wind shifts, darkening outflow clouds, dropping temperatures or declining group judgment—to abort early.

objective: Translate forecast alert tiers and field observations into timely stop, shelter or retreat actions.
applies: Outdoor travel and household emergency monitoring under changing storm, flood, wind, cold or wildfire conditions.
equipment: Weather alert receiver, local map showing exits and shelters, watch and written group turnaround limits.

failure.text: Waiting for rain or debris to strike before leaving a ridge, creek bed or exposed trail, or confusing a Watch with routine weather.

verify.text: The group can state the exact threshold that shifts the plan from continue to shorten, shelter or evacuate.

stop.text: When an active Warning or deteriorating field condition outpaces your return route, stop advancing and commit immediately to the safest reachable refuge.

title: Build an accessible emergency and evacuation plan
origin: Ready.gov People with Disabilities; new manuscript

action.text: Build a personal support network of at least three trusted contacts who know your plan, supply locations, mobility aids and communication preferences.
Arrange accessible evacuation transportation ahead of time and check whether local emergency management offers voluntary registries or utility priority-restoration lists.
Pack a go-bag and shelter-in-place kit with written prescriptions, device specs, backup power, spare eyewear or hearing batteries and service-animal food and water.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Account for mobility, sensory, medical, power and service-animal needs before an emergency disrupts daily support.
applies: Individuals and groups with disabilities, chronic medical conditions, older adults or temporary mobility limits in home or travel settings.
equipment: Personal support network list, medication and dosage card, backup power or spare batteries, accessible transport contacts and service-animal supplies.

failure.text: Assuming standard evacuation shelters, public buses or unassisted foot routes can accommodate wheelchairs, oxygen concentrators, deaf/blind alerting or service animals.

verify.text: Review and rehearse the plan with your support network, confirming backup power duration and two accessible exit routes from home or camp.

stop.text: If power-dependent medical equipment approaches reserve limits or accessible evacuation routes are threatened, activate emergency medical or local assistance early.

title: Stabilize an unexpected overnight or multi-day delay
origin: NWS winter, NPS Ten Essentials and Ready.gov kit; new manuscript

action.text: Stop travel well before dark while energy and judgment remain intact, selecting a safe, dry, sheltered position clear of flood, tree and traffic hazards.
Establish immediate exposure control—wind barrier, dry ground insulation and dry rest layers—before spending effort on secondary tasks.
Inventory safe water, food, battery charge and medication across expected delay hours, assigning scheduled check-ins and conserving energy and heat.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Shift from travel mode to sustained shelter, hydration, warmth and accountability during an unplanned night or prolonged emergency.
applies: Stranded travelers, overdue hikers or households facing multi-day disruption where immediate rescue or restoration is delayed.
equipment: Shelter and ground insulation, dry spare layers, safe water supply, lighting, communication device and emergency food.

failure.text: Pushing into darkness until exhausted, neglecting ground insulation until shivering begins, or draining phone batteries on futile searches for signal.

verify.text: Every occupant has wind/ground protection, reachable exit lighting, a rationed water plan and a scheduled communication or signaling window.

stop.text: Worsening confusion, hypothermia, heat stroke, severe dehydration or an unsafe shelter site requires immediate escalation to emergency services.

title: Decide early when storm or wildfire threatens the route
origin: NWS wildfire, thunderstorm and Ready.gov evacuation; new manuscript

action.text: Monitor wind direction, smoke plumes, storm outflow gusts and official evacuation notices to keep at least two exit paths open away from the hazard.
Evacuate early along open official routes when wildfire approaches or Red Flag winds threaten your corridor; do not wait for flames or roadblocks.
If a severe thunderstorm or tornado warning intercepts you, abandon tents and exposed timber immediately for the lowest interior room of a sturdy building or hard-topped vehicle for lightning.

objective: Choose timely exit routes and hazard-specific refuge when severe storms or wildfire develop near camp or travel corridors.
applies: Outdoor travel or rural camp exposed to approaching severe thunderstorms, straight-line winds, tornado warnings or wildfire smoke and spread.
equipment: Official alert receiver, map showing multiple road or trail exits, respiratory/eye protection if smoke is present and vehicle or go-bag.

failure.text: Waiting to pack nonessential camp gear while smoke thickens, wind topples trees or a single exit road closes behind the party.

verify.text: Everyone knows the immediate departure trigger, which gear is left behind if ordered out and the designated safe rally destination.

stop.text: Never drive or walk through active flames, downed power lines, flooded crossings or zero-visibility smoke; follow emergency responder directions immediately.

title: Adapt the plan when a companion cannot keep pace
origin: NPS Hike Smart, ARC first aid and NPS emergency plan; new manuscript

action.text: Stop the entire group on safe ground and screen the slowed person for life-threatening distress, confusion, slurred speech, chest pain, hypothermia or heat stroke.
If no urgent red flags are present, rest in shelter, address footwear, hydration, nutrition and pack load redistribution, and reassess honestly.
Shorten the route to the nearest safe exit if recovery is incomplete; never leave an impaired or exhausted member alone to catch up later.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Distinguish manageable fatigue from medical distress and safely shorten, stabilize or escalate the trip.
applies: Any group outing where one participant slows sharply, develops pain or injury, or shows early signs of cold, heat or altitude illness.
equipment: First-aid kit, spare layers, safe water, communication device and offline map showing nearest bailout exits.

failure.text: Splitting the group so faster members push to the summit while a fatigued or confused companion falls behind unobserved.

verify.text: The affected person speaks clearly, moves steadily after rest and agrees with the revised exit or hold plan.

stop.text: Confusion, stumbling, inability to bear weight, severe pain, heat stroke or hypothermia requires stopping travel immediately and activating 911 or SAR.

title: Recognize and recover from core gear failure
origin: NPS Ten Essentials, CDC filter limits and Ready.gov kit; new manuscript

action.text: Watch for early failure cues—dimming headlamp, phone battery drop in cold, frozen water filter, jammed stove valve or torn shelter anchor.
Pause on safe ground and switch immediately to your independent backup system rather than improvising hazardous repairs under stress.
Recalculate your safety margin once a primary system fails; a trip relying on its last backup is a cue to turn back or stabilize early.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Spot silent or sudden failure of lighting, navigation, water treatment or shelter gear and shift safely to backups.
applies: Field travel or home emergencies when primary equipment breaks, freezes, leaks or loses power.
equipment: Redundant core gear (backup light, paper map, secondary water method, repair tape and emergency shelter).

failure.text: Continuing deeper into remote terrain after losing primary light, offline navigation, shelter integrity or water treatment without a working backup.

verify.text: Confirm the backup system functions cleanly right now and that the revised route matches your remaining safety margin.

stop.text: When both primary and backup systems for warmth, shelter, navigation or water fail, halt onward travel, protect the group and seek assistance.

title: Reject unsafe shelter sites

action.text: Check land rules and choose an established or designated site when required. Inspect the site and access route before unpacking.
Leave stream channels, low ground that can flood and other routes concentrating runoff. Upstream rain can reach a site even when the local sky is clear.
Scan overhead and upslope. Leave any spot where loose limbs, loose material or an unstable slope threaten the group.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Rule out unsafe sites before judging comfort or convenience.
applies: Choosing temporary cover or a permitted campsite on land. Site rules and local hazards vary.
equipment: Map and weather information if available. Use daylight for inspection where possible.

verify.text: Identify an exit to safer ground and a place for the party away from overhead hazards and drainage paths.

stop.text: Reject a site if you cannot confirm a clear exit or if runoff, wind or falling material threatens it.

title: Block wind before building a roof

action.text: Choose the sheltered side of an existing stable barrier. Check that you remain clear of runoff and falling material.
Keep the exit easy to reach. Put on dry layers and protect yourself from the ground while conditions allow.
Reassess as wind direction or drifting changes. Seek a safer shelter if the barrier no longer works.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending

applies: Cold wind or blowing snow. Stable site already selected.
equipment: Existing wind barrier, insulating layers and optional shelter material made for outdoor use.

verify.text: Group members can move out without climbing over a barrier. Clothing and bedding are staying dry.

stop.text: Leave unstable cover or a blocked exit. Keep fuel-burning equipment outside enclosed shelters.

diagram: Wind | Stable barrier | Sheltered side and clear exit
visual: Side view showing windward exposure and leeward waiting position with an open exit.

title: Make a dry insulated bed

action.text: Select ground away from runoff and above standing water. Keep dry gear out of splash and wet snow.
Place dry insulation between body and ground. Add dry layers above and keep protection available for wind and precipitation.
Check for gaps under the body and wet material after settling. Replace wet insulation or move if the site is deteriorating.

applies: Short-term rest outdoors on a safe, dry site.
equipment: Camping pad or other dry insulating layer, dry clothing and weather cover if available.

verify.text: The body is separated from cold ground and the bedding stays dry where the person rests.

stop.text: If the person becomes confused, very drowsy or loses coordination after cold exposure, seek help promptly.

title: Pitch a purpose-made shelter
origin: B012 P12 and B003 tarp plate

action.text: Pick a legal durable site outside runoff channels and clear of overhead hazards. Check the immediate weather before setting up.
Assemble the shelter according to its instructions. Keep exits and equipment access clear and avoid putting wet gear on dry bedding.
Inspect all attachment points and observe how the shelter responds to wind. Adjust within manufacturer limits or relocate to suitable shelter.

applies: A commercial tent or tarp in its intended weather range on a permitted site.
equipment: Shelter, parts and instructions for the exact model; dry pad and insulation.

verify.text: The shelter remains stable, rain drains away from the bed, and each occupant can exit without unfastening gear.

title: Leave a drainage channel early
origin: B012 P09 and agency flood guide

action.text: Look for connected low ground and a clear route to higher ground. Study upstream conditions as part of the decision.
Select a higher, stable site away from streambeds and gullies. Be ready to move if warnings, rising water or new runoff appear.
Leave early by a safe route to higher ground. Follow local emergency directions.

objective: Recognize where moving water will concentrate before precipitation reaches the site.
applies: Campsites and travel near creeks, gullies, marsh edges and valley bottoms.
equipment: Map, weather alerts and a light if available.

verify.text: Someone in the group can identify both the hazard path and the exit without entering the drainage.

verify.text: Both the start and first checkpoint can be described in a way another party can use.

stop.text: If the start or route is uncertain, revise the plan before leaving known ground.

diagram: Match the trailhead | Predict first checkpoint | Compare on arrival
visual: Practice schematic with abstract checkpoints. Use actual park maps for field exercises.

title: Test offline maps and paper backup
origin: B014 reconstruction · continuation of r01

action.text: Obtain a current map that includes the planned route, nearby alternatives and identifiable roads or exits.
Disconnect the device from the network at home and open the full planned area. Confirm landmarks and scale remain readable.
Carry a paper map and use it to point to the same trailhead and route. Practice sharing a last confirmed position from paper.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Verify the route remains usable without coverage or power.
applies: Before a trip beyond dependable network service.
equipment: Downloaded map, map reader, paper map and independent power if used.

verify.text: The party can find the trailhead and two checkpoints using either map without network access.

stop.text: If the plan depends entirely on a device you cannot use offline, revise the route or kit before leaving.

diagram: Save relevant map area | Test without coverage | Match paper backup
visual: Independent map materials support the same route and landmarks.

title: Check carbon monoxide alarms before an outage
origin: Preparedness primer reconstruction · Home Resilience

action.text: Check whether there are CO alarms on each level and outside sleeping areas. Follow placement and maintenance instructions for each unit.
Check the test and backup-power procedure. Identify the agreed outdoor meeting point and make it known to everyone in the household.
If an alarm indicates carbon monoxide or exposure is suspected, get to fresh air immediately and contact emergency services.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Verify audible alarms and a family response before portable fuel equipment is needed.
applies: Household outage preparation and suspected carbon monoxide exposure.
equipment: CO alarms, exact manufacturer instructions and a household exit plan.

verify.text: The household knows the alarm sound, exit and where to call from outside.

stop.text: A working alarm does not make indoor generator or camp-stove use safe.

diagram: Verify alarms | Agree on exit | Fresh air and emergency help
visual: Prevention and evacuation checklist for a household rather than an alarm installation drawing.
reviewer: Carbon monoxide safety and emergency management

title: Match preservation plans to tested recipes
origin: Preparedness primer reconstruction · Small Acreage Self-Reliance

action.text: Find a tested recipe for the exact food and preparation. Distinguish low-acid foods that require a tested pressure-canning process from foods with other tested processes.
Match the jar size, ingredients and equipment to the recipe. Obtain its altitude adjustment before beginning.
If the recipe or equipment does not cover your ingredients, elevation or container, choose a different tested recipe or another approved preservation method.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Identify the exact tested process before preparing produce for shelf-stable storage.
applies: Household home canning. This card selects an authoritative recipe and gives no processing schedule.
equipment: Validated recipe for the food, container size and equipment. Determine local elevation.

verify.text: The recipe citation, equipment, jar size and altitude instructions agree before processing.

stop.text: Do not improvise processing time, pressure or ingredients to salvage an untested recipe.

diagram: Identify food and recipe | Confirm equipment and jar | Check altitude
visual: Canning process selection only; validated instructions control the actual process.

title: Track cold food during a power outage
origin: Preparedness primer reconstruction · Thirty-Day Outage Operations

action.text: Note when power went out and keep doors closed. A closed refrigerator typically preserves safe conditions for about four hours.
Check temperatures and elapsed time using the official chart. A closed full freezer generally holds temperature about 48 hours and a half-full one about 24 hours.
Evaluate each food by its category and storage history. For applicable frozen foods, ice crystals or a confirmed temperature of 40°F or below inform refreezing.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Use elapsed time and actual temperature to decide whether food can be kept.
applies: A household refrigerator or freezer initially working when the power fails.
equipment: Appliance thermometer, written outage log and access to the official per-item chart.

verify.text: Record the measured temperature and keep, refreeze or discard decision for each relevant food group.

stop.text: Never taste food to decide whether it is safe after a loss of cold storage.

diagram: Record power-off time | Keep doors closed | Apply official food chart
visual: Time and measured temperature together inform the per-item decision.
